summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend E2E validation of the Razorpay AI Finance Controller / Reconciliation Control Tower. Wrote pytest suite covering 18 backend cases (auth, RBAC, batch demo, reconciliation, exceptions, AI analyze via Claude Sonnet 4.6, maker-checker override with controller approval, copilot, reports, audit, model invocations, policies) — 18/18 PASS. Playwright drove login (all 4 demo buttons + typed support login), Dashboard, Batches, Reconciliation Workbench (36 rows, evidence drawer with Source A/B/C, Pass 1 confidence 100%), Exceptions (9 seeded exceptions, opened drawer, ran AI Analysis which returned MEDIUM severity triage + reviewer copilot explanation), Copilot Q&A, Reports (acceptance gates all green, value-at-risk by merchant/rail, 9-item ledger), Audit Logs (Decision Timeline + Model Invocations tabs), Admin/Policies (matching-policy editor + v1/v2 version history + roles + pending approvals), theme toggle, and logout — all functional.

ui_bugs.issue: Admin / Policies nav item is visible to ALL roles (analyst, controller, compliance, support). Support is read-only and should not see the admin route in nav; analyst also should not. Backend correctly returns 403 on POST /api/policies so functional safety is intact, but the UI leaks the entry point.

Only 4 demo account buttons rendered (Analyst, Controller, Compliance, Admin). Support role has to be typed manually (no data-testid="demo-support"). Minor UX gap given seed includes support@recon.io.

issues: Recharts logs repeated warnings 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' on initial render, indicating the ResponsiveContainer briefly gets a 0/negative parent size. Charts do render correctly after layout settles but console noise + potential FOUC on slow connections. Add minHeight/minWidth or explicit height to chart containers.

action_items: Hide/route-guard the 'Admin / Policies' sidebar item so it only appears for role in ('admin','controller'). Ideally hide from analyst/compliance/support.
Optionally add a 'demo-support' button on the login page for parity with the other seeded roles.
Fix Recharts container sizing warnings on Dashboard (set explicit height or minWidth on the chart wrapper).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is monolithic — worth splitting into routers (auth, batches, reconciliation, exceptions, copilot, reports, audit, policies) for maintainability.
Frontend does not enforce role-based nav visibility (nav items are rendered from a static array in AppShell.js regardless of user.role). Add a role filter to the nav array.
Chart containers should have deterministic sizing to avoid the width(-1)/height(-1) Recharts warnings observed on Dashboard.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (2 minor issues: RBAC nav leak, missing support demo button)

test_credentials: analyst@recon.io/analyst123, controller@recon.io/controller123, compliance@recon.io/compliance123, admin@recon.io/admin123, support@recon.io/support123 — all seed logins verified working.
seed_data_creation: Ran POST /api/batches/run-demo which seeded 3 ledgers (A/B/C) and produced ~9 exceptions across MISSING_IN_BANK, MISSING_IN_LEDGER, AMOUNT_MISMATCH, DUPLICATE, UNIDENTIFIED_CREDIT. Reused across all tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite lives at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py — run with `pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v`. It uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL and hits Claude for /exceptions/{id}/analyze and /copilot/ask (adds ~12s runtime). Sidebar test-ids are generated from labels: nav-overview, nav-batches, nav-reconciliation-workbench, nav-exceptions, nav-reports, nav-audit-logs, nav-copilot, nav-admin-policies (NOT nav-workbench/nav-audit as stated in the request context). If retesting RBAC UI fix, verify admin nav is hidden for support/analyst/compliance and visible for admin/controller.
rca of the issue: RBAC nav leak — AppShell.js renders a static navItems array with no filter by user.role. Fix: after fetching /api/auth/me, filter navItems (e.g., admin route only when role in ['admin','controller']). Backend authorization is already correct (require_roles decorator returns 403), so this is purely a UI visibility issue.
